questions.prompt: A thread computes a 4×8 tile of C. Shared loads per FMA (one load per value)?
Why must A's tile be stored transposed in shared memory for ldg4(sA, k * BM + tr) to work?
options: So a thread's 4 values from column k of A are contiguous, readable as one 16-byte load

questions.prompt: What is the main cost of an 8×8 thread tile?
options: Many registers per thread, so fewer resident warps (and bigger block tiles, so fewer blocks)
questions.explanation: Registers and parallelism pay for the reuse.

questions.prompt: Why is lower occupancy acceptable for a register-tiled GEMM?
options: Each warp has many independent FMAs (ILP), so fewer warps still keep units busy

questions.prompt: Which levels make up the GEMM tiling hierarchy?
questions.explanation: Block, warp and thread tiles; the grid is just how blocks cover C.
